The FDA can suspend certification service to a company if it appears to the Commissioner that the person has: (1) obtained or attempted to obtain a certificate through fraud or misrepresentation of a material fact; (2) falsified records required to be kept under § 80.39; (3) failed to keep such records, make them available, or allow inventory checks as required by § 80.39; or (4) refused to permit duly authorized FDA employees free access to manufacturing facilities, processes, and formulae involved in the manufacture of color additives and intermediates from which such color additives are derived [1]. The grounds for suspension are specifically listed in 21 CFR 80.34(a)(1) through (a)(4), with each condition being a basis upon which the Commissioner may suspend certification service. A person who contests the suspension has an opportunity for a regulatory hearing before the FDA pursuant to part 16 of this chapter [6].

21 CFR 80.34(a)(1): The FDA can suspend certification service if it appears that a person obtained or attempted to obtain a certificate through fraud or misrepresentation of a material fact [2].  
21 CFR 80.34(a)(2): The FDA can suspend certification service if the person falsified the records required to be kept under § 80.39 [3].  
21 CFR 80.34(a)(3): The FDA can suspend certification service if the person failed to keep such records, make them available, or allow full opportunity for inventory checks as required by § 80.39 [4].  
21 CFR 80.34(a)(4): The FDA can suspend certification service if the person refused to permit duly authorized FDA employees free access to all manufacturing facilities, processes, and formulae involved in the manufacture of color additives and intermediates from which such color additives are derived [5].  
21 CFR 80.34(b): Any person who contests a suspension of service has an opportunity for a regulatory hearing before the FDA pursuant to part 16 of this chapter [6].
